executive_summary: Iteration 000037 is functionally complete. All five user stories (US-001 through US-005) fully comply with their acceptance criteria: the default playlist is auto-created, recordings are auto-uploaded on completion, playlists can be renamed, users can create and switch between playlists, and tracks support play/download/delete with confirmation dialogs. The backend REST API (7 endpoints), service logic, and frontend state management are all correctly implemented and integrated. Two functional requirements show partial compliance on architectural naming conventions: FR-9 specifies a dedicated `playlist-panel.tsx` component (the panel is inlined in App.tsx instead), and FR-11 specifies routes in `backend/routes/playlists.py` and file I/O in `backend/repositories/playlist_repository.py` (routes live in `api.py` and file I/O is co-located in `playlist_service.py`). These deviations are structural rather than functional and do not impede any user-facing behaviour.

verificationByFR.note: Playlist metadata is persisted to `backend/playlists.json` as a JSON array of objects with id (UUID), name, and a tracks array containing id, filename, created_at, and size_bytes.
Video files are saved to `backend/recordings/{playlist_id}/{track_id}.mp4`; directories are created on demand by the service layer.
GET /api/playlists is implemented; it returns all playlists and auto-creates a default 'My Playlist' if none exist.
POST /api/playlists accepts an optional name (defaults to 'New Playlist'), persists the new playlist, and returns the created object.
PATCH /api/playlists/{id} updates the playlist name in playlists.json and returns the updated playlist object; returns 404 if the playlist does not exist.

POST /api/playlists/{id}/tracks accepts multipart/form-data with the MP4 file, saves it to disk, appends track metadata to playlists.json, and returns the new track object. Returns 400 for empty uploads and 404 for unknown playlists.
GET /api/playlists/{id}/tracks/{track_id}/file streams the MP4 file using FastAPI FileResponse with media_type='video/mp4'. Returns 404 if the playlist, track metadata, or file on disk is missing.
DELETE /api/playlists/{id}/tracks/{track_id} removes the MP4 file from disk and the entry from playlists.json; returns 204 No Content. Returns 404 for unknown playlist or track.

The playlist panel functionality is fully implemented (correct position, fetches and displays the active playlist, all track actions work), but it is inlined in App.tsx rather than extracted into a dedicated `playlist-panel.tsx` component. No `recording-queue.tsx` file existed to replace. Functional behaviour complies; the structural/file-level requirement does not.
activePlaylistId is tracked in React state in App.tsx and is initialised to the first playlist returned by GET /api/playlists on mount. Subsequent recordings and track fetches use this value.

Service logic is correctly isolated in `backend/services/playlist_service.py`. However, routes are registered in `backend/routes/api.py` (not `playlists.py`), and there is no `backend/repositories/playlist_repository.py` — file I/O helpers (_read_store, _write_store, _normalize_*) are private functions within the service module. The layering principle is respected conceptually but the prescribed file names were not followed.

verificationByUS.note: AC01–AC05 all satisfied: GET /api/playlists creates and returns a default 'My Playlist' with a UUID when none exist; the playlist is persisted to playlists.json; the frontend displays the name in the playlist header on load.

AC01–AC06 all satisfied: use-recorder.ts posts the MP4 blob to POST /api/playlists/{id}/tracks using the active playlist ID; the backend saves the file and appends metadata; the new track appears in the UI via the onPlaylistTrackUploaded callback; upload errors are surfaced via a visible red alert (playlistTrackUploadError).

AC01–AC06 all satisfied: a pencil-icon rename button is visible in the playlist header; submitting sends PATCH /api/playlists/{id}; the backend updates playlists.json and returns the updated playlist; the new name is reflected immediately and persists after reload.

AC01–AC06 all satisfied: a 'New Playlist' button POSTs to /api/playlists; a dropdown selector lists all playlists; selecting a playlist sets it as active and fetches its tracks from GET /api/playlists/{id}/tracks; subsequent recordings are uploaded to the active playlist.

AC01–AC07 all satisfied: each track row shows filename, size in MB, created_at timestamp, and Play/Download/Delete buttons; Play toggles a video element sourced from the file endpoint; Download uses the native download attribute; Delete shows window.confirm() before sending DELETE; the track disappears from the UI immediately after deletion.

minorObservations: FR-11 deviation — file I/O helpers are private functions in playlist_service.py rather than a dedicated playlist_repository.py. While the conceptual layering is correct, the prescribed file structure is not followed, which could make the codebase harder to navigate as the service grows.

FR-9 deviation — the playlist panel is inlined in App.tsx (lines ~1831–2146) rather than extracted into playlist-panel.tsx. App.tsx is already large (2400+ lines); extracting the panel would improve maintainability.

window.confirm() is used for the track-deletion confirmation dialog (US-005-AC05). This satisfies the requirement but is not theming-consistent with the rest of the app, which uses custom-styled UI components. A themed modal would be preferable.
The playlist rename input auto-saves on blur (in addition to Enter), which may cause accidental saves if focus is lost unexpectedly. The behaviour is functional but could be surprising to users.
No concurrent write protection for playlists.json. This is acceptable for a single-user desktop context but worth noting for future multi-session scenarios.

UI: The playlist selector is a native <select> element. While functional and accessible, it is visually inconsistent with the custom-styled controls elsewhere in the app. A styled dropdown would improve theming consistency.
UX: There is no visual empty-state illustration or call-to-action for an empty playlist beyond a text message, which is a missed opportunity to guide new users.
conclusionsAndRecommendations: The iteration delivers full functional value across all five user stories with no gaps in user-facing behaviour. Both partial-compliance findings (FR-9 and FR-11) are architectural rather than functional: the prescribed component and file names were not used, but the code is correctly structured conceptually. Recommended actions: (1) Extract the playlist panel from App.tsx into a dedicated `src/components/playlist-panel.tsx` to reduce file size and match the PRD spec. (2) Move file I/O helpers from `playlist_service.py` into `backend/repositories/playlist_repository.py` and move playlist route handlers from `api.py` into `backend/routes/playlists.py` to align with FR-11. (3) Replace window.confirm() with a themed in-app confirmation dialog for track deletion. These are low-risk refactors that improve long-term maintainability without changing any user-visible behaviour.
